anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Only publication moved, and it moved as intended. Before failed it because its PUBLISH block passed `--base "$DEFAULT"` inherited from the separate PROOF sequence, minted the body file via `$SCRATCH`, and had the equality retry re-run 'only the gh pr create line', which inherits TITLE and DEFAULT from an earlier shell. After fixes this with a single self-contained CREATE call: it reads the committed H1 into TITLE in that same call, passes the observed base as the literal 'main', and names the literal body-file path that mktemp printed and the file writer used; the retry then refers back to that whole block. PUSH is split out, so the retry cannot re-push, and the body with its bare EOF line is still written as data by the file writer rather than a heredoc. No fact that Before kept was lost. To keep it that way, keep the wording that makes CREATE one fresh-shell call with a literal base and path, and keep the explicit 'No amend and no push' on the retry. Three small things could be tightened: the BASE step still shows a `DEFAULT=$(...)` assignment that nothing later uses and could be read as shell-state reliance; the mint output is abbreviated as `.../pr-body.Q7rT2k` and would be safer printed in full so the same-path match is unambiguous; and the two retry gates are merged into one block, so render them separately if the case's 'independently' is to be honoured literally. The flagged reply would also be safer if it kept the word 'malformed'.
